snip.t: The findings point to the rare testicular feminization (androgen insensitivity syndrome), with a karyotype of 46, XY.
Androgen insensitivity syndrome: 46,XY karyotype, tissues cannot respond to androgens → phenotypically female external appearance, primary amenorrhea, presents in adolescence.

snip.t: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS): Genetic defect in androgen receptors, causing XY individuals to develop female external genitalia despite normal or high testosterone levels.

qs.q: An XY embryo with androgen insensitivity syndrome will develop which gonads?
o: A single ovotestis in every case
qs.e: An XY individual with androgen insensitivity develops testes because testicular differentiation is driven by the Y-chromosome pathway. The androgen receptor defect prevents normal androgen effects on target tissues.
